correctness.rationale: A pairwise-intersecting two-set collection is either contained in a star, or exactly a triangle: edges ab and ac together with an edge not using a force bc, after which no fourth edge is possible. This yields the disjoint zero-support counts, taking care that the empty and singleton cases do not have a unique center. For a fixed zero support, inclusion–exclusion imposes absence of each named color in each specified open neighborhood; an outside edge can carry a color exactly when it intersects every zero edge in that color's failure set. A double label has the conjunction and weight 2, so each factor and the weighted sum agree. A minimum can have weight N−(n−1) only with a full zero star and singletons outside. It is attained even at n=5 by using distinct disjoint perfect matchings on four noncentral points, one per color. In any singleton split, a star zero {c,i} sees a color precisely when some edge of that color avoids i. For a fixed bad color the allowed subsets of a single star count as one empty, binom(m,2) singles and m times the at-least-two subsets of m−1 edges, m=n−1. Both colors cannot fail because two star centers leave at least two vertices outside their union of centers. This proves the minimum formula, classifier, counts and full polynomial under the named-color convention.
residual_risks: Full coefficient checks are finite; all-n validity is supplied by the support classification and event identity.
